title: Guidelines for Employers' Use of Automated Decision-making Tools for Hiring or Promotions to Prevent Biases
what_it_is: Guidelines for Employers' Use of Automated Decision-making Tools for Hiring or Promotions to Prevent Biases

sections.label: AI discrimination complaints to TAFEP
sections.summary: Workers facing AI-related discriminatory employment practices can seek TAFEP help, and TAFEP has received no such complaints to date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: If certain artificial intelligence (AI) use results in discriminatory employment practices, workers or job applicants can approach the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) for assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: TAFEP will work with the employer to address the grievances of the workers or job applicants and ensure that the employer’s recruitment or performance appraisal processes adhere to the principles of fair employment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To date, TAFEP has not received complaints of discrimination arising from the use of AI tools.

sections.label: Monitoring AI adoption trends
sections.summary: The Government will monitor AI adoption trends and work with tripartite partners to assess if existing guidelines and regulations are adequate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to closely monitor the trends in AI adoption and work with our tripartite partners, the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) and the broader HR community to regularly assess if existing guidelines and regulations are adequate.

sections.label: Encouraging employees to raise concerns
sections.summary: Asked what new approaches MOM would consider to encourage employees to raise concerns, the speaker notes employer power imbalance and employee advantages in a tight labour market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, in that context, where there is always a power imbalance and there is always information asymmetry in favour of an employer, what new approaches would the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) consider to encourage employees to raise concerns to, say, TAFEP or to any other appropriate authority in MOM?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think that it is important to recognise that in today's climate, depending on which aspects that you are looking at, the employee also has certain advantages vis-à-vis choosing the choice of employers that they want to work for, because we do have a very tight labour market.

sections.label: Handling complaints expeditiously
sections.summary: Every complaint and question is dealt with expeditiously and transparently, and a database of complaint types would sharpen employee protection while maintaining balance for employers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Of course, we cannot take things for granted because we continue to work hard at tripartism, at working with the different chambers to achieve this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But I want to reassure the Leader that every single complaint and every single question is dealt with expeditiously in a very clear and transparent manner.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And by building a database, a repository of the nature of the different types of complaints, it would sharpen our ability to protect employees better and, at the same time, maintain that balance for employers.
